object_description: Cloverleaf-shaped single-storey volume around a central circulation space
design_condition: The compact cloverleaf volume aligns its south-east facade with the street, freeing the central south-east zone for shared reception and public access while placing sports and recreation areas at the foot of the hill.

positive.statement: The project cleverly takes possession of the site through its street alignment and compact footprint.

position.rationale: The compact cloverleaf mass visibly aligns its south-east edge with the street side.

positive.statement: The arrangement reorganizes the exterior spaces and frees the central zone for reception, recreation and public access.

position.target: central reception, recreation and public access zone
position.rationale: The central articulation visibly opens toward the south-east access side.

positive.statement: The built volume clearly expresses the functions it houses.

position.rationale: The articulated three-branch envelope provides the anchor for functional expression.

positive.statement: The central space immediately accessible from the entrance organizes the three units.

position.rationale: A central articulation is clearly visible where the three branches meet.

positive.statement: The green roof is treated as a true fifth facade and is widely readable from the pedestrian link.

position.rationale: The roof footprint is clearly readable from above and forms the visible fifth facade.

positive.statement: The concept clearly defines three major outdoor spaces.

position.rationale: Three exterior pockets are visibly formed between the cloverleaf branches.

positive.statement: The supporting wooden frame provides appropriate spans for the chosen material.

position.rationale: The frame is not individually visible; the eastern branch provides a representative surface anchor.

positive.statement: Wood and single-level construction are relevant for the poor bearing capacity of the soil.

position.rationale: Single-level massing is visible, while material and soil suitability remain constrained.

positive.statement: The project meets fire quality assurance requirements on a single level.

position.target: fire quality assurance on a single level
position.rationale: The one-storey envelope is visible, but fire compliance itself lacks a distinct marker.

negative.statement: The outdoor activity areas must be physically demarcated for rational use, reducing the relevance of the proposed exterior developments.

position.rationale: Branch-separated exterior pockets are visibly assigned as distinct activity areas.

negative.statement: The structural system is complicated and its changes in portico orientation weaken the central articulation.

position.rationale: Structural changes are not individually visible; the central articulation is the likely focus.

negative.statement: Winter operation is problematic because circulation to the three zones is too narrow or constricted.

position.rationale: The central connector visibly mediates routes to the three branches.

negative.statement: The central spaces in the three zones are unattractive or undersized.

position.target: central spaces in the three zones
position.rationale: Interior-facing central pockets are visibly narrow and irregular around the articulation.

negative.statement: The seismic safety device is not indicated, and the cloverleaf geometry requires numerous interior walls to control torsional effects.

position.rationale: The device is absent from the sample; the central mass is the most plausible structural anchor.

negative.statement: A complete second-level extension would probably require deep foundations.

position.rationale: The model is single-storey, so a second level can only be assigned to the existing roof footprint.

negative.statement: The scheme raises problems with escape-route distances if the building is elevated.

position.rationale: Escape routes are not visible; the street-facing south-east access edge provides a directional anchor.
